messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary group canary-42 reporting progressive memory growth and increasing tail latency. 95th p95 trending up 4x in 10m. Automated rollback check ran but no action taken (threshold not breached).
Alex: seeing same on dashboards — mem RSS creeping, GC spikes, 5xx rate up ~3.8% on canary routes. not cluster-wide yet.
Priya: paging oncall. I'm taking lead. we should consider manual rollback if this keeps ramping. @morgan can you check recent image or config changes for canary-42?
Morgan: no config pushed in last 2hrs. quick grep of recent builds shows a tiny runtime change landed with new kv-prefetch flag, but it was only enabled on canary. that could explain cache pressure.
Sam: if it's the kv-prefetch flag we can flip it off via feature flag service quickly. alternatively we can roll the canary back. which path do we want?
Priya: flip flag first (lower blast), then if latency doesn't drop within 3 mins -> manual rollback. Sam do the flag flip + start draining to 0 traffic proactively.
Sam: flipping flag now -> `featureflip set kv-prefetch false --env=prod --target=canary-42`
Sam: (reaction) :white_check_mark: flag flip pushed
Alex: seeing initial drop in allocations but tail latency still high. mem growth slowed a bit. 2m in, p95 down 15% but errors still ~2.2%.
Priya: that's borderline. @morgan + @sam start manual rollback prep in parallel. call the rollback but don't cut traffic until we have coord ok. Morgan, can you capture heap/profile before we drain?
Morgan: collecting heap snapshot now — saving to s3://redwood-incidents/canary-42/6112233445-heap.hprof
Sam: starting graceful drain of canary-42 hosts (scale to 0) now. running command: 
```
redwoodctl rollout drain --canary canary-42 --grace-period 60s
```
Sam: drain started, connections being drained. will wait for in-flight to finish then trigger rollback.
Priya: Ops checklist: 1) notify customers (support), 2) notify platform leads, 3) execute rollback, 4) smoke tests, 5) verify SLOs. @lia can you draft the support note?
Lia: drafting now. short note to customers: "We observed increased latency and transient errors for a small percentage of requests to our inference endpoint. We are rolling back a canary deployment and expect service to normalize within 10–15 minutes."
ci-cd-bot: Starting rollback pipeline for canary-42 (initiated by sam). pipeline id: rb-202611223-01. logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/pipelines/rb-202611223-01
Sam: executing rollback command: 
```
redwoodctl rollback --deployment canary-42 --target-version v2.14.1
```
Sam: rollback in progress. will stream status.
ci-cd-bot: Rollback job rb-202611223-01: step 1 completed (scale down canary). step 2: promote previous stable version -> in progress.
Alex: observing immediate drop in 5xx after first scale down. throughput shift to stable nodes is working.
Priya: once rollback done, run quick smoke on `/health` and `/v1/generate` sample prompts. Morgan keep an eye on mem and GC. Lia monitor customer replies.
ci-cd-bot: Rollback job rb-202611223-01: completed successfully. promoted v2.14.1.
Sam: rollback finished. all canary hosts removed.
Lia: smoke tests: `/health` 200 OK from 8 regions, sample inference prompt returned in ~120ms median. posting gist of checks: https://gist.redwood/internal/6112233445-smoke
Morgan: mem trend returned to baseline within 3 minutes of rollback. GC spikes cleared. seemed correlated with kv-prefetch path. saving traces and heap for followup.
Alex: error rate back to ~0.1% (normal). no customer escalations yet but Support flagged ~12 timeouts during the 8–12 minute window.
Priya: customer impact summary: small cohort (canary traffic) experienced elevated latency and ~12 timeouts for a subset of customers, duration ~8–12m. no major data loss. reopening postmortem ticket to investigate kv-prefetch flag interaction.
Sam: reopening the canary testcases in staging to reproduce. will add tighter auto-rollback thresholds for mem and tail latency.
Lia: support message sent to affected customers, flagged for follow-up with eng if they report ongoing issues.
Priya: good work. we'll hand off to the morning oncall with notes: root suspicion = kv-prefetch flag; data collected: heap, traces, rollback pipeline id rb-202611223-01, smoke gist. closing thread but monitoring for 1hr. :white_check_mark:
